requestedActions.title: List file and folder names in the app folder, including continuation until all entries are listed

prohibitions: Uploading, editing, moving, or deleting files or folders
guide.summary: Dropbox documents per-user OAuth 2.0 access for User API endpoints. The list-folder endpoint requires files.metadata.read, and list_folder/continue uses the same scope for pagination while has_more is true. App Folder is an app-level content-access option that limits actions to /apps data; it is not a separate grant. The app must be registered in the App Console and use a code flow with a client secret, or PKCE for public clients. Each customer consents on the Dropbox authorization page, and review may be affected by scope requests. Review timing and distribution to other customer workspaces remain unknown.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth code flow issues a user-associated token
findings.detail: Apps requesting only User API scopes receive a token associated with the authorizing user. The code flow redirects the user to dropbox.com for authorization, then exchanges the returned code at /oauth2/token with the client secret. This matches the confirmed per-account OAuth request and excludes team tokens.
findings.appliesWhen: The app uses OAuth for each individual customer account with no team administration.

findings.title: files.metadata.read covers listing file and folder entries in the app folder
findings.detail: The list_folder and list_folder/continue endpoints require files.metadata.read and accept user tokens. The App Folder content-access option limits actions allowed by the scopes to data within the app folder (/apps). The scope does not itself restrict folder location, and this is the least-privilege documented scope for read-only metadata listing.
findings.appliesWhen: The request lists names of entries in the customer app folder and continues pagination until has_more is false.

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Exchange the authorization code for a user access token
Done when: The token endpoint returns an access_token and expires_in for the test user. The access token is stored server-side and is not logged.

List the first page of app folder entries
Done when: The response returns a JSON object with entries (name and .tag), cursor and has_more. Entry names are displayed; no file content is downloaded. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Continue listing until has_more is false
Done when: Pagination ends when a response returns has_more=false; the combined entries from all pages are collected. Continuation was executed on at least one page when has_more was true. A response returns has_more=false and all pages have been collected.

Confirm the grant does not allow content download or file changes
Done when: The request log shows only list_folder and list_folder/continue calls, and the token's granted scope is files.metadata.read.
